subject: Orthosys capacity sync: tokens/sec targets & preliminary fleet plan
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-17T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Orthosys capacity sync: tokens/sec targets & preliminary fleet plan

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, Orthosys is targeting a real-time inference footprint for the new chat assistant plus an asynchronous batch pipeline for analytics. To make the Dedicated sizing concrete for the proposal, can you confirm the following so we model a realistic fleet plan: 

- Expected steady-state tokens/sec during business hours (UTC-7): estimate and 95th percentile burst.
- Desired P95 generation latency SLO for the chat flow (you mentioned ~250–350ms target range).
- Ratio of real-time requests to batch inference (sample: 70/30).
- Peak concurrent users and avg tokens per request for chat (approx).

I've attached a quick starter workbook (orthosys_tps_model.xlsx) with token-rate assumptions and a handful of fleet tiling scenarios (A100x8, A100x16, A10G mixes, and a quantized CPU fallback lane). The workbook has slots for you to fill the numbers; we'll use that to size a committed slab and define an ops plan for burst lanes.

Proposed next steps:
1) You fill the yellow fields in the workbook with your best estimates.
2) We run a short internal sizing with Engineering (compute/tps mapping + headroom) and return a recommended Dedicated slab + suggested canary rollout.
3) Align on SLA targets and a mutually agreed mutual-action plan (MAP) for rollout and procurement.

Would you be available for a 30-min follow-up tomorrow afternoon (US-PST)?

Thanks,

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Stephanie —

Appreciate the recap and the workbook. Quick answers below to unblock sizing: 

- Steady-state tokens/sec (business hours): ~18,000 tokens/sec.
- 95th percentile burst: ~55,000 tokens/sec (during product demos and overnight batch flushes)
- P95 latency target for chat: 300ms (hard SLO for demo users; soft SLO for internal traffic)
- Real-time vs batch: ~65% real-time chat / 35% batch analytics
- Peak concurrent users: 3,200 active chat sessions; avg tokens per request: 45 tokens (short prompts + short responses)

I've uploaded a short note from our infra team describing some traffic seasonality (demo spikes around product launches). Will get procurement on the thread if we move to a committed contract.

Happy to join a follow-up tomorrow at 3pm PST.

— Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-18T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: quick sizing pass for Orthosys (estimates)

Folks —

I ran a short mapping using Alex's numbers. Notes and conservative assumptions below so Sales/Eng can align on a recommendation. This is an internal pre-read; please don't forward yet.

Assumptions used
- Chat P95 target: 300ms
- Steady tokens/sec: 18k, 95th burst: 55k
- Avg tokens/request: 45
- Real-time ratio 65% -> effective real-time tokens/sec: 11.7k steady / 35.75k burst

Per-GPU throughput (approx; depends on model family & quantization):
- A100 (80GB): 6,000 tokens/sec per GPU (fp16, default kernel selection)
- A10G: 1,900 tokens/sec per GPU (mixed precision)
- T4-like: 900 tokens/sec per GPU (quantized, cost-optimized)

Sizing scenarios (rounded):
1) Low-latency heavy: target P95 300ms with 1.8x headroom -> require sustained capacity ~21k tokens/sec -> if using A100s: 4 GPUs (6k ea -> 24k) + 1 canary/ops buffer -> recommend Dedicated slab = 8x A100 (allows burst and cross-zone redundancy).
2) Mixed-cost blend: committed slab 12x A10G (gives ~22.8k sustained) + short-term burst pool of 4x A100 for demo spikes.
3) Cost-minimized: 30x T4-style GPUs to cover steady-state only (27k) but risky on tail latency (less headroom).

Operational considerations:
- KV cache warmup: chat workloads with long context will require pre-warmed KV cache — plan for a caching layer + warmup script in rollout.
- Canary: route 5% traffic through Dedicated slab initially; monitor p95 & errors for 72 hours before ramp.
- Fallback: configure a quantized CPU lane or hosted fallback for degraded GPUs during peaking events to avoid hard errors.

Recommendation for commercial packaging:
- Propose a 12-month committed slab combining A10G baseline + 4 A100 burst nodes, with a 15% burst buffer credit line. Price to include 24/7 premium support during the first 90 days of ramp.

I'll join the customer sync at 3pm PST to present this.

-Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Alex / team —

Thanks for the fast replies and for joining the afternoon session. Based on your traffic profile and our internal sizing pass (summary below), here's a recommended approach we can put into the MAP and SPA: 

Executive summary (recommended):
- Committed slab: 12x A10G GPUs (baseline sustained ~22.8k tokens/sec).
- Burst pool: 4x A100 GPUs reserved for demo windows and high-priority spikes (brings burst capacity to ~46.8k tokens/sec).
- Headroom: targets ~1.35x steady-state headroom (sits between cost & latency protection). This meets your 300ms P95 in our simulation with KV caching enabled and model quantization for non-demo traffic.

Key operational pieces:
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% over 3 days with rollback hooks.
- Monitoring: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, and token consumption per minute; we will share a dashboard with token and cost breakouts.
- Cache warming: warmup during canary & before major demo windows; engineering will provide a warmup script.

Commercial ask & next steps:
- Deal ID: ORTH-2025-0917-1. Proposed term: 12 months committed baseline + on-demand burst credits.
- Procurement: Maya / procurement@orthosys.ai, can you confirm the billing contact and preferred contracting doc (they prefer redlined MSA or PO-first)?
- Deliverables from Redwood: sla_proposal_v1.pdf (attached), final compute tiling workbook (we'll update orthosys_tps_model.xlsx with the agreed numbers), and a MAP with dates for canary and GA.

If this matches, I'll kick off the commercial paperwork and loop Solutions Engineering to finalize the deployment runbook.
